title: market channel v2 — registry fields, chart slots (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support/auth_ok.support (capability id afbws.market.channel.v2). Second generation of the `market` channel; afbws.market.channel.v1 stays available next to it until the frontend has fully migrated, the backend chooses the generation per connection by `auth.support` only (a client may declare both ids during the migration; there is no version-gated behaviour). Every instrument is addressed by the catalog's full `instrument_key` (see common.v1.json#/$defs/instrumentKey), never a bare SECID. ONE schema id per message (`afbws.market.<op>.v2`): the same schema is the reply to a request (carries `request_id`) and an unsolicited push to a live subscription (no `request_id`) — deliberately no `.request`/`.response`/`.push` suffixes. Messages: `subscribe`/`subscription` (replace-all quotes subscription), `get` (one request, `target` = series|quotes|fields), `series` (candles plus requested data fields, columnar), `quotes` (cross-instrument quote rows), `fields` (which data fields exist for an instrument), `source_status` (health push) and `error`. DATA FIELDS. Instead of closed per-kind column lists, a client asks for concrete fields named `<source>.<field>` (e.g. `trades.val_b`), optionally with a rolling-median suffix `@median(N)`. The protocol fixes only the NAME SHAPE (pattern on `get.fields`); which source/field/median combinations are valid is decided by the server's field registry, so a new field of an existing source needs no protocol change. A requested field that the server cannot serve is not an error: it is listed in `series.unavailable` with a reason and the rest is delivered. `get` with target=fields tells a client what the registry offers for one instrument. CHART SLOTS. A chart page has up to two charts; each is a `slot` (0 or 1). `slot` is mandatory in `get` (target=series) and in `series`: there is no default. A connection has at most one live series subscription PER SLOT (so at most two); a live `get` replaces only the subscription of its own slot, `superseded` acts inside the slot only, a history `get` touches no subscription, and there is no explicit unsubscribe — a subscription lives until a live `get` of the same slot replaces it or the connection closes (a client that switched a slot off simply ignores its pushes). Identical (instrument, period, fields) sets in two slots are two independent subscriptions. QUOTES. `subscribe` is explicit and replace-all (the client states its whole desired set every time); `get` (target=quotes) is the one-shot variant. The quote column set is fixed by the schema. `NaN` never appears on the wire — sources that produce it are converted to `null`. See AFB/docs/ws/market.v2.md.

slot.description: Chart slot (two charts on a page). In `get` (target=series) it names the slot whose live subscription this request may replace; in `series` it is the echo of the request's slot (reply) or the slot of the subscription (merge push), by which the client routes a push to the right chart.

fieldRequest.description: `<source>.<field>` with an optional `@median(N)` suffix, N an integer 1..999 by shape (the real upper bound is `fields.median_max_days`, enforced by the server). `@median(N)`: N is the width in CALENDAR DAYS of a rolling window before the bar's date; for a bar of date D and in-day slot s the value is the median of the same field in the same slot s over the days [D-N, D) — the current day D is excluded, days without a value are skipped, no values means null. Defined for intraday periods and `1d` (for `1d` the slot is the whole day); other periods answer the field as `unavailable` (`not_supported`). The response column is named `<field>@median(N)` (without the source prefix).

unavailableEntry.title: One `series.unavailable[]` element — a requested field the server did not deliver.

field.description: The requested field exactly as sent in `get.fields`.

reason.description: `unknown` — no such source/field in the registry. `not_applicable` — the field exists but not for this instrument/market. `no_access` — the caller's access does not include this source. `not_supported` — the field has no median (or no such mode), or the period / N is outside what the registry supports for it.

table.title: Columnar data block of one source for a `series`.
table.description: `columns` lists `time` first (UTC unix seconds = the candle's timestamp), then field names WITHOUT the source prefix, with the `@median(N)` suffix where one was requested. A client reads by column name, never by position. `rows` hold only numbers and `null` (NaN is sent as `null`), each row as long as `columns`. Rows exist only at the timestamps of the candles of the SAME message (the `candles` table is the grid): the server aligns every source to it; there are no rows outside trading hours and no forward-filled values.

source.description: `candles` or a source name of the server's field registry (the part of `get.fields` before the dot).

resolved_key.description: Present only when the server substituted the source instrument (e.g. a stock or a broker-only instrument of an asset resolved to its derivative for positions). Absent means the requested `instrument_key` itself was used.

rows.description: Each row has the same length and column order as `columns`.

candlesTable.title: The candles table: always `tables[0]` of a series.

dataTable.title: A non-candle table of a series (`source` is never `candles`).

dataStatus.title: Degraded-data marker.
dataStatus.description: Present on a `series` message only when it is NOT a normal fresh answer: either the external source's circuit breaker was open when it was built (served from the cache only, no network; the `candles` table may then be shorter or missing) or the freshness detector found the instrument's data lagging behind a live market while the fetch itself nominally succeeded. Absent means a normal, fresh answer.

state.description: "partial": at least one requested table could not be served at all. "stale": every requested table is present but may lag behind the live market.

source.description: Which external source this is attributed to.

since.description: When this degraded condition started, ISO-8601 with offset.

series.title: afbws.market.series.v2 — candles of one instrument plus the requested data fields.
series.description: Reply to `get` (target=series) when `request_id` is present — `mode:"replace"`, the full requested range; the client replaces its copy of this slot's instrument+period range with `tables`. Unsolicited push to the slot's live subscription when `request_id` is absent — `mode:"merge"`: rows only at the timestamp(s) of the latest candle(s) (the just-closed bar plus the new one on a period rollover), upserted by `time`. `tables[0]` is ALWAYS the candles table (source `candles`, columns `time, open, high, low, close, volume`) — the grid every other table is aligned to; further tables follow, one per requested source that delivered at least one field. Fields that were requested but not delivered are listed in `unavailable`. A failure to load the candles themselves is NOT answered with a `series` but with `error` (`provider_error`, `timeout` or `not_supported`) and creates no live subscription; a failed merge-push update is simply not sent (freshness is reported by `data_status`). There is no free-text `message` here.

mode.description: "replace": the full answer to a `get`. "merge": a live push — rows only at the latest candle time(s).

unavailable.description: Optional: requested fields that are not in `tables`, with the reason. Absent when everything requested was delivered.

future_times.description: Optional, live series only: UTC unix seconds of the opening tick of each future (not-yet-formed) `period` bar after the last candle in `tables`, per the trading calendar — strictly increasing, no duplicates. Computed server-side; there is no client-side calendar lookup. Present on the `mode:"replace"` reply to a live `get` and re-sent on a `mode:"merge"` push only when the list actually changed — a `merge` push without `future_times` means it is unchanged. Never present on a pure history fetch (`end_date` strictly before today). Rendered as whitespace bar slots past the last real candle.

quotes.title: afbws.market.quotes.v2 — cross-instrument quote rows.
quotes.description: Reply to `get` (target=quotes) when `request_id` is present (always `mode:"full"`); unsolicited push to the connection's quotes subscription when it is absent: `mode:"full"` right after `subscribe`, then `mode:"update"` with only the rows that changed (about every 30 s). `columns` is fixed by the schema (`instrument_key, last, close, percent, volume`); adding a column is a protocol PATCH. Each row is keyed by its first column, `instrument_key`.

mode.description: "full": the client replaces its whole quote cache (reply to `get`, first push after `subscribe`). "update": only the changed rows; the client upserts them by `instrument_key`.

rows.description: Each row follows `columns`: instrument_key (string), then last, close, percent, volume (number or null).

fieldEntry.title: One field of a source in `fields.sources[].fields[]`.

name.description: Field name; the client requests it as `<source>.<name>`. Stored and computed fields are not distinguished.

median.description: True when `@median(N)` is allowed for this field.

fieldSource.title: One data source applicable to the instrument, as seen by the caller.

resolved_key.description: Present only when the source instrument differs from the requested one (same meaning as `table.resolved_key`).

step_sec.description: Native step of the source's data in seconds (currently 300 or 86400). Deliberately not a closed enum: a source with another native step is a registry row on the server, not a protocol change.

fields.title: afbws.market.fields.v2 — data fields available for one instrument.
fields.description: Reply to `get` (target=fields); always carries `request_id`. `sources` lists only the sources that are applicable to the instrument AND available to the caller (a source the caller has no access to is omitted, not marked).

median_max_days.description: Upper bound of N in `@median(N)` (calendar days).

subscribe.title: afbws.market.subscribe.v2 — replace-all quotes subscription (client -> server).
subscribe.description: The client states its whole desired set of instruments every time; the server does not diff against a previous `subscribe`. An empty `instrument_keys` unsubscribes. Reply is `subscription` with the same `request_id`, immediately followed by a `quotes` push with `mode:"full"`. Does not affect the series subscriptions, those are driven by `get` (target=series) alone.

subscription.title: afbws.market.subscription.v2 — accepted quotes subscription, reply to subscribe.v2.
subscription.description: `instrument_keys` is the accepted subset of what was requested; `rejected` lists the instruments that could not be subscribed with a reason code. Always followed by a `quotes` push with `mode:"full"`.

get.title: afbws.market.get.v2 — one-shot request (client -> server); `target` selects the kind.
get.description: Reply by `target`: series -> `series` (mode:"replace"), quotes -> `quotes` (mode:"full"), fields -> `fields`; or `error` — all with the same `request_id`. Each target allows only its own fields (the others are rejected by the schema). target=series: candles are ALWAYS delivered (they are the grid the data rows live on, there is no flag for it); `fields` asks for additional data fields (see `$defs/fieldRequest`), its validity is decided by the server registry and an unserved field lands in `series.unavailable` instead of failing the request. LIVE RULE: if `end_date` is absent, or not earlier than "today" in the instrument's market timezone, this request ALSO becomes the live series subscription OF ITS `slot` and replaces only that slot's previous subscription (the replaced live `get`, if still pending, is answered with `error` code `superseded`); the server then pushes `series` (mode:"merge") for it. A request with `end_date` strictly before today (history paging) is a pure history fetch and touches no subscription. A connection has at most one live series subscription per slot, so at most two; there is no explicit unsubscribe — it lives until replaced by a live `get` of the same slot or until the connection closes. Identical sets in the two slots are two independent subscriptions. The limit of concurrently running heavy `get`s per connection is unchanged and applies across slots (`busy`). target=quotes: `instrument_keys` omitted means all instruments with cached data. target=fields: the answer lists the registry's sources and fields for the instrument.

start_date.description: target=series only: first date to fetch, YYYY-MM-DD in the instrument's market timezone.

end_date.description: target=series only: last date to fetch, YYYY-MM-DD; omitted means up to the latest available. Also decides whether this request becomes the slot's live subscription — see the parent description.

fields.description: target=series only: data fields to deliver next to the candles; omitted means candles only. A `@median(N)` request widens the data read backwards by N days on the server; the answer still covers only the requested range.

instrument_keys.description: target=quotes only: instruments to fetch; omitted means every instrument with cached data.

sourceStatusEntry.title: One `source_status.sources[]` element — one external source's current health.

source.description: External source name as tracked by the backend's health registry.

since.description: When this source entered its CURRENT state, ISO-8601 with offset.

reason.description: Human-readable cause (window error rate/p90 for degraded, breaker cooldown for down).

sourceStatus.title: afbws.market.source_status.v2 — health snapshot of the backend's external data sources.
sourceStatus.description: Unsolicited push, no `request_id`: sent on each health-state transition of an external source and once as a full snapshot right after this channel's first `subscribe`/`get`. `sources` lists every source the backend currently tracks; a source absent from the list has never reported a call yet — treat as "ok". Same structure as v1.

error.title: afbws.market.error.v2
error.description: Reply to a failed `get` (same `request_id`) or a channel-level error. Codes are the v1 codes plus the candle-load failures `provider_error` and `timeout`. `superseded` — a live `get` (target=series) was cancelled because a newer live `get` of the SAME slot replaced it before it finished; the client discards the pending request silently. `busy` — the connection's concurrent heavy-`get` limit was exceeded or the server is under memory pressure; carries `retry_after_sec`. `provider_error` — loading the candles failed at the data provider (the reason is in `message`; no live subscription was created). `timeout` — loading the candles timed out (same consequences). `not_supported` — the period or the instrument is not supported by the candle source (also used for an unsupported period of a data source).

retry_after_sec.description: code=busy only: seconds the client should wait before retrying the same request once.

errorCode.description: Own enum of this channel (not common.v1.json#/$defs/errorCode, so that v1 does not widen): the common codes plus `provider_error` and `timeout`.
